title: MPI-safe field sampling and engineering postprocessing
summary: Evaluates fields at common physical points, polylines and planar sections with deterministic MPI ownership; compares fields across meshes, extracts strong-constraint force/moment resultants, and selects retained accepted frames.

science.statement: A finite-element field is evaluated inside a containing owned cell from its basis representation; distributed ownership changes where evaluation occurs, not the returned physical value order.

equations.label: finite-element point evaluation
equations.description: The containing cell supplies the local basis functions and coefficients for the requested physical point.

equations.label: path coordinate
equations.description: Polyline vertices define cumulative arc length; samples are uniformly spaced along this coordinate.

equations.label: discrete reaction moment
equations.description: Owned discrete residual entries are paired with nodal coordinates; MPI reduction counts no ghost forces twice.

inputs.name: field
inputs.type: DOLFINx scalar, vector, or tensor Function
inputs.description: The finite-element field whose coefficients and function space define the interpolation.

inputs.name: physical coordinates
inputs.description: Coordinates in the mesh geometric dimension, supplied identically on every MPI rank.

outputs.name: point values
outputs.description: Values are returned in request order and replicated consistently on every rank.

outputs.name: path sample
outputs.description: Can be attached directly to SimulationResult as a named distance history.

assumptions: Every MPI rank calls the sampler collectively with identical coordinates.
The requested point lies in the physical mesh unless missing='nan' is selected explicitly.
A one-sided discontinuous value is sampled inside the intended cell rather than exactly on its interface.
conventions: The lowest-rank owned-cell candidate evaluates a point; ties on one rank use the lowest local cell index.
Missing points raise by default instead of silently returning zero.
Path distance is cumulative physical arc length from the first endpoint.
Accepted-frame history requests use physical time or normalized load factor; an unlabelled frame sequence must provide its coordinate explicitly.
Transient requests are evaluated only after accepted increments and are restored through the shared checkpoint history.
One online transient history channel is scalar; vector or tensor sensors use explicit components or separate named channels.
applicability: Final-state quantities of interest, line plots, campaign outputs, sensor comparisons, compact digital-twin observations, and observation data for learned models.
limitations: Segments and polylines are built in; general curved paths should supply explicit coordinates to sample_points.
Interface traces of discontinuous fields require an explicit one-sided sampling location.
Planar section samples are point observations, not cut-cell quadrature or area averages.
Field comparison uses explicit common physical locations; its sample norms are not volume norms.
Reaction moments use owned discrete residuals on Cartesian nodal spaces and the reference geometry.
Accepted snapshot selection reads retained fields only and does not reconstruct missing states.
Online transient requests store compact scalar histories, not a replacement for spatial field-output frames.

usage.minimal_example: sensor = results.probe_history('tip_U2', at=(L, H/2), component=1, unit='m'); result = step.solve_result(output='results.xdmf', history=(sensor,))

tasks.title: 空间测点与时间历史 / point history
tasks.prerequisites: SI linear Newmark structural-dynamics project; initialize with dynamic-results template.
tasks.limitations: History uses accepted physical time in seconds, independently of sparse cloud frames. For load-factor paths use task:load-path.

validation_rules: Reject negative geometric padding, unknown missing-point policies, and coordinates with the wrong geometric dimension.
Reject rank-inconsistent coordinate requests before field evaluation.
Check polyline arc length, scalar/vector/tensor plane samples and partial mesh coverage against exact affine fields.
Check support force and moment against independent equilibrium for first- and second-order cantilever meshes.
Check retained nonlinear frames against the independent homogeneous StVK nominal stress relation without changing the final live field.
Reject missing points before returning a scientific quantity unless missing='nan' is explicit.
Reject duplicate or conflicting transient history names and non-scalar online channels.
Reject continuation when the accepted-history channel schema differs from the checkpoint evidence.
